decision.summary: Two regions stand out: (1) a correlated multi-sample dip in N/E/U near indices 490–510, possibly a transient offset with partial return; (2) a sharp, symmetric V-shaped excursion across all axes from 725 to 729, indicating a brief but coherent displacement event. Other intervals show typical noise or smooth trends without ambiguous superposed changes.

regions.observation: N/E/U components show a correlated multi-sample drop around index 495–505, with N and U decreasing together while E shows a shallower dip; the shape suggests a possible transient offset or co-located motion, not fully resolved by coarse sampling—surroundings show return toward prior trend by ~510.

From ~725 onward, all three axes exhibit a clear V-shaped excursion: N drops then recovers, E drops more sharply then recovers, and U drops then rises steeply; the symmetry and alignment across axes suggest a short-duration physical displacement or instrumental artifact, with full recovery visible by 729.
